Nevertheless, international geopolitical tensions and fluctuating commodity prices present daunting challenges. Cutting sweet foods doesn’t curb cravings or improve health
items.content: Changing how much sweet-tasting food people eat may not change how much they crave or enjoy sweetness after all. In a six-month trial, researchers found that people assigned to high-, low-, or average-sweetness diets showed no meaningful differences in their preference for sweet foods, body weight, or markers linked to diabetes and heart disease. Many participants also drifted back toward their previous eating habits once the trial ended.

items.title: Meteorite that smashed through a New Jersey roof reveals clues to life’s origins
items.content: A rare meteorite that crashed through a New Jersey roof contains evidence of ancient salty fluids, organic compounds, and amino acids from a primitive asteroid. Its pristine chemistry could offer new clues about how space rocks helped supply early Earth with some of the ingredients needed for life.
